title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan

epigraph.quote: Acknowledge both the engine and the brakes: a great business at a stretched multiple requires trimming overweight risk, not abandoning discipline.
epigraph.author: Portfolio Risk Committee

web_blocks.html: Our synthesis separates two distinct decisions that investors routinely conflate: (1) whether new capital should buy SEDEMAC at ₹3,129.10, and (2) what to do with our existing 200-share Zerodha holding (cost ₹4,05,098.25 / ₹2,025.49 per share; market value ₹6,25,820.00; unrealized gain +₹2,20,721.75 or +54.49%; portfolio weight 14.56%). On the Bull side, SEDEMAC is a genuine COMPOUNDER_PASS with patented sensorless ISG/EFI IP, 35.3% ROCE, 40%+ H1 FY27 revenue growth, and a textbook Stage 2 VCP base (7.2% Bollinger bandwidth) backed by rising FII ownership (10.30%) [1, 5, 10, 11, 22]. On the Bear side, TVS Motor represents ~75–81% of revenue, FY26 Free Cash Flow was -₹47 Cr, Sep 2026 borrowings jumped nearly 5x to ₹352 Cr, H1 FY27 OPM slipped to 19.2%, and 107.0x trailing P/E prices in ~28% annual compounding for a decade [1, 5, 6, 14].

web_blocks.caption: Both Sides of the Aisle: Bull vs. Bear Steelman & Independent Judgment
rows: Granted US/global patents on sensorless ISG/EFI eliminate Hall-effect sensors, cutting BOM cost and raising OEM switching costs [10, 11].

Real IP moat in 2W/3W ISG and ~75% genset AMF share; earns COMPOUNDER_PASS.
Bajaj Auto, Hero MotoCorp, and Generac exports are scaling to diversify away from TVS Motor over FY27–FY29 [13].
TVS Motor still drives ~75–81% of revenue (top-3 >90%), giving TVS massive pricing and dual-sourcing leverage [6, 14].
Concentration remains the #1 fundamental risk; demands a <10% portfolio weight cap.
MF3 (120k sq ft Chakan) and MF5 (13 acres Shoolagiri) add multi-year capacity as MF1 hit >90% utilization [5].
FY26 FCF was -₹47 Cr, Debtor Days stretched to 46.1, and Sep 2026 debt surged 5x to ₹352 Cr for capex & chip inventory [1, 5].
Growth-led capex is strategic, but negative FCF and debt jump block new capital at 107x P/E.
Operating leverage on 40%+ top-line growth lifted OPM from 12% (FY21) to 20% (FY26) [1].
Over 70% of RM is semiconductor/PCB-linked; H1 FY27 OPM slipped 220 bps YoY to 19.2% on component inflation [5, 14].
Model 19.0–19.5% steady EBITDA margins rather than extrapolating peak 21%+ quarters.
Stage 2 VCP coil (7.2% BB width, 10W EMA ₹3,116.67) with FIIs quadrupling stake to 10.30% [1, 22].
107.0x TTM P/E and 26.5x P/B already price in ~28% 10Y CAGR; Base fair value ₹3,050 is below CMP.
REJECT new capital; TRIM_OVERWEIGHT 100 of 200 shares while holding 100 core shares.
web_blocks.takeaway: We respect the Bull case's IP and weekly 30W SMA support by keeping 100 core shares, while respecting the Bear case's 107x valuation and concentration risk by rejecting new capital and trimming 100 overweight shares.

web_blocks.html: Action Triggers: Trim 100 shares at CMP (≥₹3,129.10) to cut weight from 14.56% to ~7.28%. Trim 30 more at ₹3,650.00. Exit all 100 remaining shares on a daily close below ₹2,696.82.

Our execution discipline is anchored in clear, pre-committed price triggers rather than emotional reactions to intraday noise. Trimming 100 shares at or above ₹3,129.10 cuts single-stock exposure in half to 7.28%. Keeping 100 core shares preserves exposure to any Stage 2 VCP breakout toward Pivot R1 (₹3,509.40) and ₹3,650.00. If price closes below our ₹2,696.82 hard invalidation stop (below the 30-week SMA at ₹2,757.91), we exit all remaining 100 shares [22].

We also preserve clear criteria for revisiting SEDEMAC with fresh capital in future quarters. A pullback toward ₹2,050–₹2,400 would reset the forward P/E into a 45x–55x range. Alternatively, consecutive quarters of >20% EBITDA margins, positive Free Cash Flow, and Bajaj/Hero volume scaling that lowers TVS Motor's share below 60% would improve fundamental durability. Until those gates clear, fresh cash earns better risk-adjusted returns in MANORAMA and liquid reserves.

book_paragraphs: We have reached the moment of truth—where every hour spent reading patents, checking debtor days, and tracing Reverse DCF math has to crystallize into a clear, unhedged decision. Notice how cleanly our two-pass discipline protects us from emotional traps: Pass 1 confirmed that SEDEMAC is a genuine technological compounder, while Pass 2 proved that at ₹3,129.10 and 107x trailing earnings, the stock offers no margin of safety for fresh capital.

Let's put both sides of the aisle on the table and weigh them honestly. The Bull case rests on rare IP and accelerating scale: SEDEMAC owns patented sensorless ISG and EFI control electronics, commands ~75% of Indian genset AMF controllers, grew revenue 41% YoY in H1 FY27 to ₹710 Cr, and just printed a 35.3% ROCE. Foreign institutional investors have quadrupled their stake to 10.30%, and the daily chart is coiling in a tight Stage 2 VCP box right on the 10-week EMA.

The Bear case is equally concrete and cannot be waved away. First, 75% to 81% of SEDEMAC's revenue still flows through a single customer, TVS Motor. Second, the company burned -₹47 Cr of Free Cash Flow in FY26, stretched debtor days from 24 to 46.1, and increased borrowings nearly fivefold from ₹72 Cr to ₹352 Cr by September 2026 to fund MF3, Shoolagiri (MF5), and semiconductor buffer inventory. Third, at 107x trailing P/E, the market is already pricing in ~28% annual compounding for ten straight years—while our 45x Bear FY28E multiple implies ₹1,679 (-46.3%), pulling probability-weighted 12-month expected value down to ₹2,907.25 (-7.09% below today's price).

Under our Anti-Hedging Rule, we refuse to hide behind a timid 'Wait for Support' label when even the support band fails the math. Our Base Case 12-month fair value is ₹3,050—which sits *below* the ₹3,069.92–₹3,175.62 support zone. Even if the stock pulls back to ₹3,120, you do not have 1.5:1 reward-to-risk against the ₹2,696.82 invalidation stop. Therefore, our new-capital verdict across Short-Term, Medium-Term, and Long-Term horizons is **REJECTED** (driven by **VALUATION** and **CASH_FLOW**).

Now, what about the 200 shares you and I already own in Zerodha? Those 200 shares were acquired at an average cost of ₹2,025.49 (total cost ₹4,05,098.25) and are worth ₹6,25,820.00 today—a +54.49% gain and a massive **14.56% portfolio weight**, making SEDEMAC the single largest equity position in the entire Indian account.

Think about the portfolio-level risk of leaving 14.56% of your Indian equity capital in one stock whose revenue is 75% to 81% tied to TVS Motor and whose stock trades at 107x trailing earnings. If TVS Motor delays a model launch, dual-sources an ISG platform, or squeezes vendor margins during a 2W slowdown, a 46% Bear multiple compression in SEDEMAC would single-handedly erase nearly 7% of total portfolio value.

At the same time, because weekly structure still holds above the 30-week SMA (₹2,757.91) and Bollinger bandwidth has squeezed to 7.2%, dumping all 200 shares would be just as undisciplined as buying more at 107x P/E—yet the flat-to-falling 50-DMA (₹3,138.55) and 8 recent distribution days argue for cutting overweight exposure in half. Therefore, our holding action is **TRIM_OVERWEIGHT**: sell **100 shares** at or above ₹3,129.10 (~₹3,12,910 proceeds, locking in ~₹1,10,361 of profit) to bring SEDEMAC down from 14.56% to a sensible ~7.28% core weight. Keep the remaining **100 shares** riding the weekly trend, protected by a hard daily-close stop at **₹2,696.82** and an upside profit-lock trim of 30 more shares if the stock spikes to ₹3,650.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The mark of an institutional portfolio manager is holding two true ideas at once: rejecting fresh capital at 107x P/E because expected return is negative, while trimming an overweight 14.56% winner in half to 7.28% rather than panic-selling above the 30-week SMA.

book_subsections.title: Where the Trimmed ₹3,12,910 Goes: 70% Cash, 30% MANORAMA
paragraphs: Every rupee freed by trimming 100 shares must have an explicit, ledger-verified destination. First, we retain **70%** (~₹2,19,037) in **CASH**—lifting Zerodha cash from ₹5,74,582 to ~₹7,93,619 (18.47% of the account) and respecting the market's narrow-breadth uptrend and 3 distribution days.

Second, we allocate **30%** (~₹93,873) to **MANORAMA** (`ACCUMULATE_ON_DIP` on our shortlist at ₹1,984.10, verified `Stage 2 (Markup)` in both `market_facts` and snapshot ledgers, `target_base` ₹2,650.00, offering 2.36:1 asymmetry on dips into ₹1,869.54–₹1,957.58 support). Notice why we bypass AJMERA here: although AJMERA carries an older shortlist tag, our fresh November 13 `market_facts` ledger classifies it as `Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback)` with a falling 200-DMA, so we refuse to deploy fresh cash into a Stage 3 chart.
Finally, we allocate **0%** to **OUTSIDE** peers (`UNOMINDA` at 60.9x TV / 59.9x Screener P/E and `FIEMIND` at 19.8x P/E), as neither beats our active Stage 2 shortlist setup today.

book_subsections.title: What Would Change Our Mind on New Capital
paragraphs: We never close the door on a `COMPOUNDER_PASS` business forever. Two developments would trigger a fresh re-underwrite for new capital: either a time-and-price correction that brings SEDEMAC's forward multiple down toward 45x–55x earnings (around ₹2,050–₹2,400 on current estimates), or consecutive quarters of >20% EBITDA margins paired with positive Free Cash Flow and confirmed volume diversification at Bajaj Auto and Hero MotoCorp that drops TVS concentration below 60%.

book_subsections.title: Before & After Portfolio Risk Audit: Right-Sizing from 14.56% to 7.28%
paragraphs: Let us walk through the exact portfolio arithmetic of our `TRIM_OVERWEIGHT` action in Zerodha. Before the trim, the Indian portfolio holds ₹37,22,869 in equities and ₹5,74,582 in cash (total account value ₹42,97,451), with 200 shares of SEDEMAC valued at ₹6,25,820—an outsized 14.56% weight against a cost basis of ₹4,05,098 (₹2,025.49 per share).

By selling 100 shares at ₹3,129.10, you free ₹3,12,910 of capital and realize roughly ₹1,10,361 of profit (50% of your +₹2,20,722 unrealized gain). Your remaining 100 shares carry a market value of ₹3,12,910, bringing SEDEMAC's portfolio weight down to 7.28%—cleanly inside a disciplined single-stock ceiling for a high-concentration Tier-1 supplier.

Meanwhile, retaining 70% of the freed ₹3,12,910 in Cash lifts liquid reserves to ₹7,93,619 (18.47% of the account), while rotating 30% (₹93,873) into verified Stage 2 shortlist name MANORAMA upgrades portfolio reward-to-risk: you exchange a 107x P/E position with negative incremental asymmetry for cash optionality plus a 2.36:1 Stage 2 compounder. And if SEDEMAC resolves upward toward ₹3,650, your remaining 100 shares participate in the rally while alert #2 locks in another 30 shares into euphoria.

Notice how every single piece of this plan is pre-committed before emotions take over. You do not have to guess at 9:15 AM IST when a red candle or green candle prints. If SEDEMAC trades at or above ₹3,129.10, you execute the 100-share overweight rebalance. If it breaks out on heavy volume toward ₹3,650 without an upward earnings revision, you harvest 30 more shares. And if the base fails and closes below ₹2,696.82, you exit the remaining 100 shares cleanly with your capital intact.

Let us also double-check why we do not rotate the trimmed ₹3,12,910 into Uno Minda or Fiem Industries today. Both are respectable listed peers—Uno Minda at 60.9x TV P/E (59.9x Screener) offers multi-OEM breadth across 2W and 4W platforms, while Fiem Industries at 19.8x P/E offers a 29.3% ROCE in automotive LED lighting. Yet neither sits on our active shortlist with a fresh Stage 2 entry trigger superior to MANORAMA (2.36:1 asymmetry). Keeping 70% in cash alongside that Stage 2 deployment gives us far better portfolio-level risk-adjusted upside.

Over the next four quarters, keep your eye on four decisive milestones: (1) whether TVS Motor's share of revenue begins stepping down from 75–81% as Bajaj Auto and Hero MotoCorp scale; (2) whether MF3 in Chakan ramps above 60% utilization and lifts EBITDA margins back toward 20.5%; (3) whether Debtor Days normalize below 35 days and Free Cash Flow turns positive as the semiconductor inventory buffer unwinds; and (4) whether net debt peaks near ₹352 Cr rather than climbing further. Until those milestones verify alongside a better entry multiple, our 100-share core stake is plenty.
